answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with escrowed work bonds: before handling valuable tasks, each agent must lock a bond that is slashed if independent auditors later find its work faulty. Creating many fake identities then requires funding many separate bonds, so the cost scales linearly with the attack. Over a long horizon, honest agents recover their bonds plus fees, while a terrace of escalating bond sizes for higher-value work keeps large fraud unprofitable. Public audit records act as a mirror, letting anyone check an agent's past faults before trusting it again.
